title: Senate Republicans Move Campaign Money From North Carolina to Kansas
summary:
Imagine you planned to spend your allowance on one thing, then decided to spend it somewhere else. Something like that is happening in this year's Senate elections.

The Senate Leadership Fund is a super PAC, a group that raises and spends money to help candidates win. It is linked to top Senate Republicans. On Friday, four people who know about the plan said the group is pulling back in North Carolina and buying a seven-figure amount of ads in Kansas. Seven figures means at least one million dollars. These people asked not to be named because they were talking about private strategy.

In North Carolina, the group had planned to spend $18 million on ads over the next month. It has already spent about $32 million there. The Associated Press says the shift suggests Republicans are less sure that their candidate, Michael Whatley, can beat Democrat Roy Cooper, a former governor.

Kansas has leaned Republican. Donald Trump won it by nearly 16 percentage points in the last presidential election. But the Associated Press says higher fuel costs and other money worries have made the race closer than Republicans expected. Senator Roger Marshall, a Republican, is running for another term against Democrat Adam Hamilton.

The midterm elections are on Nov. 3. They will help decide which party controls Congress. Republican campaign leaders say high fuel prices are one thing weighing on their candidates.
why_it_matters: The Senate helps decide which laws pass, so where each party spends money shows where it thinks control of Congress could be won or lost.
